the tanna who ordered the mishnayot, donkey first (chapter 1) then cow (chapter 2)
the R' Chanina who asked R' Eliezer (5b.3); כדרבי חנינא at 13a.12
transmits R' Oshaya's memra (13a.13); his own view on meshicha at 13b.3
מאן דאמר גזילו של גוי מותר (13b.6)

props.gloss_en: the tanna taught the fetus of his donkey first, and then the fetus of his cow
the West, first answer: since it is dear to him, as R' Chanina
the West, second answer: since the matters of a non-kosher animal are few, he finishes it and sets it aside
R' Eliezer (to R' Chanina): moreover, [the donkeys] helped Israel at the Exodus
a Jew who gave money to a gentile for his animal according to their laws, though he did not pull -- acquired
...and [the animal] is liable to the firstborn
a gentile who gave money to a Jew for his animal according to their laws, though he did not pull -- acquired
...and it is exempt from the firstborn
(entertained) 'according to their laws' means the laws of [the gentile's] person -- learned by kal vachomer from the purchase of his person
the verse compared [the Canaanite slave] to an achuza: as an achuza is acquired by money, document and chazaka, so a Canaanite slave is acquired by money
Abaye: 'according to their laws' means the laws the Torah set for them
Abaye: 'or buy from your fellow's hand' (Vayikra 25:14) -- from your fellow's hand it is by pulling; hence from a gentile's hand, by money
(entertained) in the second clause 'according to their laws' means the laws of [the Jew's] person -- by kal vachomer from the gentile's purchase of his person
Abaye: in the second clause too, the laws the Torah set for them
Abaye: 'and if you sell a sale to your fellow' (Vayikra 25:14) -- to your fellow by pulling; hence to a gentile, by money
Ameimar: with a gentile, pulling acquires
R' Yochanan: by Torah law money acquires; pulling does not
if Ameimar holds like R' Yochanan, לעמיתך does its work: with your fellow by money, with a gentile by pulling
Reish Lakish: pulling is explicit in the Torah
the word 'to your fellow' written in Vayikra 25:14 -- whose work 13b.3 asks for on the Reish Lakish branch
to your fellow you return overcharge (onaah); you do not return overcharge to a gentile
one [verse-word] for a gentile and one for hekdesh: there is no onaah for hekdesh either
one view: robbing a gentile is forbidden
another view: robbing a gentile is permitted
if [Ameimar] holds robbing a gentile is permitted, perforce he holds like R' Yochanan
one who buys gerutaot from gentiles and finds an idol among them: if he pulled before paying, he returns it; if he pulled after paying, he takes the benefit to the Dead Sea
the stam: the baraita speaks where [the gentile] accepted to be judged by Jewish law
Abaye: the first clause [he returns it] because it is a mistaken purchase
Rava: both clauses are mistaken purchases; in the first, not having paid, it does not look like an idol in a Jew's hand; in the latter, having paid, it does
Abaye: the latter clause is not a mistaken purchase -- having paid, when he pulled he should have inspected and then pulled
Rav Ashi: from the first clause, pulling does not acquire; so in the latter too; 'pulled' is said in the latter only because the first said it
Ravina: from the latter clause, pulling acquires; so in the first too; and the first means: if he neither paid nor pulled, he may retract -- retract in words
[the tanna] holds: [retracting] words carries [the stigma of] lacking faith -- that is, Jew from Jew, for they stand by their word
but Jew from gentiles, who do not stand by their word -- not

answered_by.gloss_en: הכי קאמר: אף על פי שנתן מעות, אי משיך -- אין, ואי לא -- לא
